column1: When Mount Pinatubo suddenly erupted on 9 June 1991, the power of volcanoes past and present again hit the headlines.
column2: 1991年6月9日，皮纳图博火山突然爆发，过去与现在的火山力量再次登上新闻头条。

column1: Volcanoes are the ultimate earth-moving machinery.
column2: 火山是地球上最强大的‘推土机’。

column1: A violent eruption can blow the top few kilometres off a mountain, scatter fine ash practically all over the globe and hurl rock fragments into the stratosphere to darken the skies a continent away.
column2: 一场猛烈的喷发可将山体顶部几公里的岩层吹飞，将细灰几乎散播至全球各地，并将岩石碎片抛入平流层，使遥远大陆上的天空变暗。

column1: But the classic eruption — cone-shaped mountain, big bang, mushroom cloud and surges of molten lava — is only a tiny part of a global story.
column2: 但那种经典的火山喷发——锥形山体、剧烈爆炸、蘑菇状云团和熔岩洪流——只是全球故事中微不足道的一小部分。

column1: Vulcanism, the name given to volcanic processes, really has shaped the world.
column2: 火山活动，即那些与火山相关的现象，确实塑造了这个世界。

column1: Eruptions have rifted continents, raised mountain chains, constructed islands and shaped the topography of the earth.
column2: 火山喷发使大陆分裂，形成山脉，创造岛屿，并塑造了地球的地形。

column1: The entire ocean floor has a basement of volcanic basalt.
column2: 整个海洋底部都有一层由火山玄武岩构成的基底。

column1: Volcanoes have not only made the continents, they are also thought to have made the world’s first stable atmosphere and provided all the water for the oceans, rivers and ice-caps.
column2: 火山不仅创造了大陆，人们认为它们还塑造了地球上第一个稳定的大气层，并提供了海洋、河流和冰盖所需的全部水分。

column1: There are now about 600 active volcanoes.
column2: 目前世界上大约有600座活跃的火山。

column1: Every year they add two or three cubic kilometres of rock to the continents.
column2: 每年，火山向大陆添加两到三立方千米的岩石。

column1: Imagine a similar number of volcanoes smoking away for the last 3,500 million years.
column2: 想象一下，在过去的35亿年里，也有数量相当的火山持续喷发着烟雾。

column1: That is enough rock to explain the continental crust.
column2: 这些岩石足以解释大陆地壳的组成。

column1: What comes out of volcanic craters is mostly gas.
column2: 火山口喷出的主要是气体。

column1: More than 90% of this gas is water vapour from the deep earth: enough to explain, over 3,500 million years, the water in the oceans.
column2: 这种气体中，超过90%是来自地下的水蒸气，足以在35亿多年的时间里解释海洋中的水量。

column1: The rest of the gas is nitrogen, carbon dioxide, sulphur dioxide, methane, ammonia and hydrogen.
column2: 其余气体是氮气、二氧化碳、二氧化硫、甲烷、氨和氢气。

column1: The quantity of these gases, again multiplied over 3,500 million years, is enough to explain the mass of the world’s atmosphere.
column2: 这些气体的总量，在35亿年的时间里累积起来，足以解释地球大气的质量。

column1: We are alive because volcanoes provided the soil, air and water we need.
column2: 我们能够存活下来，是因为火山为我们提供了所需的土壤、空气和水资源。

column1: Geologists consider the earth as having a molten core, surrounded by a semi-molten mantle and a brittle, outer skin.
column2: 地质学家认为，地球有一个熔融的核心，周围包裹着半熔融的地幔，而最外层则是一种脆弱的结构。

column1: It helps to think of a soft-boiled egg with a runny yolk, a firm but squishy white and a hard shell.
column2: 可以把一个溏心蛋的蛋黄流质、蛋白柔软有弹性、外壳坚硬的形象，当作理解火山的比喻。

column1: If the shell is even slightly cracked during boiling, the white material bubbles out and sets like a tiny mountain chain over the crack — like an archipelago of volcanic islands such as the Hawaiian Islands.
column2: 如果外壳在沸腾时哪怕有微小裂纹，白色物质就会冒出并凝固，形成类似小型山脉的构造——就像夏威夷群岛那样的火山岛群一样。

column1: But the earth is so much bigger and the mantle below is so much hotter.
column2: 但是地球的体积要大得多，而且地幔的温度也要高得多。

column1: Even though the mantle rocks are kept solid by overlying pressure, they can still slowly ‘flow’ like thick treacle.
column2: 尽管地幔岩石因上覆压力而保持固态，它们仍能缓慢地像浓稠的糖浆一样流动。

column1: The flow, thought to be in the form of convection currents, is powerful enough to fracture the ‘eggshell’ of the crust into plates, and keep them bumping and grinding against each other, or even overlapping, at the rate of a few centimetres a year.
column2: 这种流动被认为是以对流的形式存在的，其力量足以将地壳的‘蛋壳’结构破坏成多个板块，并使这些板块以每年几厘米的速度相互碰撞、摩擦，甚至重叠在一起。

column1: These fracture zones, where the collisions occur, are where earthquakes happen.
column2: 这些断层带正是地震发生的区域，碰撞事件也在这里发生。

column1: And, very often, volcanoes.
column2: 而且，往往都是火山。

column1: These zones are lines of weakness, or hot spots.
column2: 这些区域是薄弱地带，或是热点地区。

column1: Every eruption is different, but put at its simplest, where there are weaknesses, rocks deep in the mantle, heated to 1,350°C, will start to expand and rise.
column2: 每次火山喷发都不同，但最简单来说，当地幔深处的岩石被加热至1350°C时，若存在薄弱点，就会开始膨胀并上升。

column1: As they do so, the pressure drops, and they expand and become liquid and rise more swiftly.
column2: 随着压力下降，这些物质膨胀成液体并迅速上升。

column1: Sometimes it is slow: vast bubbles of magma — molten rock from the mantle —inch towards the surface, cooling slowly, to show through as granite extrusions(as on Skye, or the Great Whin Sill, the lava dyke squeezed out like toothpaste that carries part of Hadrian’s Wall in northern England).
column2: 有时候这个过程相当缓慢：巨大的岩浆泡——来自地幔的熔岩——缓缓向地表涌出，最终冷却成花岗岩。这种现象可以在斯凯岛或大威恩斯尔等地看到；那里的熔岩流就像牙膏一样被挤压出来，同时带走了英格兰北部哈德良长城的一部分结构。

column1: Sometimes — as in Northern Ireland, Wales and the Karoo in South Africa — the magma rose faster, and then flowed out horizontally on to the surface in vast thick sheets.
column2: 有时候——比如在北爱尔兰、威尔士以及南非的卡鲁地区——岩浆上升的速度会更快，然后以巨大的厚层形式水平流向地表。

column1: In the Deccan plateau in western India, there are more than two million cubic kilometres of lava, some of it 2,400 metres thick, formed over 500,000 years of slurping eruption.
column2: 在印度西部的德干高原上，有超过两百万立方千米的熔岩，其中部分厚度达2400米，这些熔岩是在超过50万年的持续喷发中形成的。

column1: Sometimes the magma moves very swiftly indeed.
column2: 有时候，岩浆移动得非常迅速。

column1: It does not have time to cool as it surges upwards.
column2: 它还没有来得及冷却，就已经向上涌升了。

column1: The gases trapped inside the boiling rock expand suddenly, the lava glows with heat, it begins to froth, and it explodes with tremendous force.
column2: 被困在沸腾岩石中的气体突然膨胀，岩浆因高温而发出光芒，并开始起泡，最终以巨大的力量爆发出来。

column1: Then the slightly cooler lava following it begins to flow over the lip of the crater.
column2: 随后，温度稍低的熔岩开始从火山口边缘流下来。

column1: It happens on Mars, it happened on the moon, it even happens on some of the moons of Jupiter and Uranus.
column2: 这种情况在火星上发生过，月球上也出现过，甚至木星和天王星的一些卫星上也有类似现象。

column1: By studying the evidence, vulcanologists can read the force of the great blasts of the past.
column2: 通过研究这些证据，火山学家能够了解过去那些巨大爆炸的威力。

column1: Is the pumice light and full of holes?
column2: 这种浮石看起来很轻，而且还有很多孔洞吧？

column1: The explosion was tremendous.
column2: 爆炸的威力非常巨大。

column1: Are the rocks heavy, with huge crystalline basalt shapes, like the Giant’s Causeway in Northern Ireland?
column2: 这些岩石是否很重？它们呈现出巨大的结晶状玄武岩形态，就像北爱尔兰的‘巨人之路’一样。

column1: It was a slow, gentle eruption.
column2: 这是一次缓慢而温和的喷发。

column1: The biggest eruptions are deep on the mid-ocean floor, where new lava is forcing the continents apart and widening the Atlantic by perhaps five centimetres a year.
column2: 最大的火山喷发通常发生在中洋底，那里新的熔岩不断将大陆分离开来，使得大西洋每年扩大约五厘米。

column1: Look at maps of volcanoes, earthquakes and island chains like the Philippines and Japan, and you can see the rough outlines of what are called tectonic plates — the plates which make up the earth’s crust and mantle.
column2: 看看火山、地震以及像菲律宾和日本这样的岛屿群的地图，你可以看到所谓的‘构造板块’的大致轮廓——这些板块构成了地壳和地幔。

column1: The most dramatic of these is the Pacific ‘ring of fire’ where there have been the most violent explosions — Mount Pinatubo near Manila, Mount St Helen’s in the Rockies and El Chichón in Mexico about a decade ago, not to mention world-shaking blasts like Krakatoa in the Sunda Straits in 1883.
column2: 其中最引人注目的就是太平洋上的‘火环’区域，那里发生过最剧烈的火山爆发——比如马尼拉附近的皮纳图博火山、落基山脉中的圣海伦斯火山，以及大约十年前墨西哥的埃尔奇琼火山。更不用说1883年巽他海峡发生的克拉卡托亚火山喷发那样震撼世界的大爆炸了。

column1: But volcanoes are not very predictable.
column2: 不过，火山的活动并不容易预测。

column1: That is because geological time is not like human time.
column2: 这是因为地质时间与人类时间不同。

column1: During quiet periods, volcanoes cap themselves with their own lava by forming a powerful cone from the molten rocks slopping over the rim of the crater; later the lava cools slowly into a huge, hard, stable plug which blocks any further eruption until the pressure below becomes irresistible.
column2: 在平静时期，火山会用自身喷发出的熔岩覆盖火山口，形成一个坚固的锥体；随后熔岩缓慢冷却，凝固成一个巨大、坚硬、稳定的堵塞物，阻止喷发，直到下方压力变得无法抗拒为止。

column1: In the case of Mount Pinatubo, this took 600 years.
column2: 以皮纳图博火山为例，这一过程持续了600年。

column1: Then, sometimes, with only a small warning, the mountain blows its top.
column2: 然后，有时仅有个微小的预警，山就会爆发。

column1: It did this at Mont Pelée in Martinique at 7.49 a.m. on 8 May, 1902.
column2: 这一事件发生在1902年5月8日清晨7点49分，地点是马提尼克岛的蒙佩莱火山。

column1: Of a town of 28,000, only two people survived.
column2: 在这座拥有28,000人口的城市中，只有两个人幸存下来。

column1: In 1815, a sudden blast removed the top 1,280 metres of Mount Tambora in Indonesia.
column2: 1815年，印度尼西亚坦博拉火山顶部1280米的岩体突然崩塌。

column1: The eruption was so fierce that dust thrown into the stratosphere darkened the skies, cancelling the following summer in Europe and North America.
column2: 这次火山喷发极其猛烈，喷出的尘埃进入平流层，使欧洲和北美的天空变暗，导致接下来的夏季无法正常进行。

column1: Thousands starved as the harvests failed, after snow in June and frosts in August.
column2: 由于六月的降雪和八月的霜冻，农作物歉收，成千上万的人因此陷入饥饿。

column1: Volcanoes are potentially world news, especially the quiet ones.
column2: 火山活动可能成为世界新闻，尤其是那些平静的火山。
